summary: Redwood AE+SE walked NovaPay through an edge-case demo focused on KV cache shedding, long context behavior and graceful timeouts under high TPS. Customer is concerned about session-state explosion, per-tenant cold misses, and streaming backpressure impacting UX. Agreed next steps: pilot with dedicated pool, share tuning docs and schedule load run.
topics: KV cache eviction and shedding strategies
Streaming backpressure and client-side retry patterns
Timeout policies and graceful degrade (model fallbacks)
Dedicated capacity vs hosted burst considerations
transcript:
[00:00] Alyssa (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. quick intro, i'm alyssa and with me is diego from our infra SE team.
[00:07] Priya (NovaPay): hey thanks, i'm priya, lead on ML infra, and ew- evan, tom and rita are on. we wanted to see how you handle the really heavy tail cases—long context and many concurrent sessions.
[00:20] Diego (Redwood SE): great, that's exactly what we planned to demo; we'll start with a short overview then jump into the console and the optimize playbook.
[00:30] Tom (NovaPay): quick note, our traffic has bursts up to ~8k rps for auth prompts and mix of short and very long contexts—some sessions hit ~50k tokens.
[00:40] Diego: ok noted, 50k is in the long tail; two important pieces: kv cache behavior and streaming backpressure handling when many sessions are active. we'll show how we shed cold keys and keep hot prefixes sticky.
[00:55] Rita (NovaPay): when you say "shed" — do you mean you evict whole sessions or selectively drop older KV entries? sometimes we can't tolerate losing the last 2k tokens.
[01:07] Diego: good Q. we do tiered eviction: soft TTL + LRU within tenant shard. we can soft-evict older blocks and keep most recent n-k tokens pinned if you pin a session. in practice you configure pinning for high-value sessions and a background compaction that snaps the KV to a condensed summary.
[01:25] Priya: that sounds like memcache style, is there a dashboard for pinning and TTLs?
[01:31] Alyssa: yes, in console -> sessions -> cache controls. we'll open it now. (screen share)
[01:40] [01:40] Diego: here is an example autoscale policy tied to queue depth and tail latency. notice the backpressure threshold hooks and the graceful-degrade rule that routes to a cheaper quantized model when latency exceeds SLO.
[01:55] Tom: so you can set a policy that if p95 > 350ms then switch replicas?
[02:01] Diego: exactly. there are preconditions for model compatibility; we automatically check tokenization and kv layout. fallback keeps the API contract identical but you may see slight quality variance.
[02:13] Evan (NovaPay): on billing, if we route to a quantized variant, is token billing affected?
[02:18] Alyssa: pricing differs by model variant, our billing records which variant served so you can split cost. we'll send a sample billing breakdown.
[02:26] [02:26] Priya: ok demo request: show us a synthetic run with a spike to 10k TPS, several long sessions, and one client doing streaming reads that can't keep up. we want to see behavior first-hand.
[02:38] Diego: perfect. i'll run a loco-like load; note that our test will exercise three levers: prefetching KV for pinned sessions, shedding cold keys under memory pressure, and stream backpressure TTLs.
[02:52] [05:10] Diego: starting the load now—watch the per-route dashboard—i'm injecting a steady 2k rps baseline and at minute 3 i'll ramp to 10k for 15 minutes.
[05:23] Priya: copying.
[06:01] [06:01] Alyssa: alert firing: queue depth rising on region-1. Diego, what's our first-level mitigation?
[06:07] Diego: two steps: we increase worker count (if dedicated autoscale allowed) and start shedding cold keys per the policy. shedding policy is conservative: evict keys older than 12 hours or compact them into a summarized prefix.
[06:20] Tom: can that compaction break session semantics for us? we have business logic that expects last-turn context.
[06:28] Diego: compaction keeps last-turn explicit; the summarization removes older system-level tokens and keeps the last n tokens intact. there's a config param 'min_recent_tokens' you can set.
[06:39] Priya: hmm ok show me the console edit.
[06:41] Diego: (edits config) setting min_recent_tokens=2048 and compaction_window=6h.
[06:48] Alyssa: while diego changes that, you'll see a slight spike in p95 as workers spin up; that's expected. watch the stream panel.
[07:00] [07:00] System: streaming backpressure rule engaged for stream-id: s4321, client reported read-slow.
[07:06] Rita: what's the user-visible effect when the stream backs up? do clients get chunked timeouts?
[07:12] Diego: we have a cooperative backpressure mechanism: we buffer small chunks for a configurable TTL (default 10s) and if client can't keep up we moderate production speed and fall back to shorter deltas. after TTL we either drop non-critical deltas or send a final partial answer with a continuation token.
[07:28] Priya: continuation token could be heavy for our mobile flows. do you support resumable sessions with delta state stored in object store?
[07:35] Diego: yes, resumable tokens map to a persisted snapshot in object store; that costs a bit of latency on resume but keeps streams small. many customers use this for mobile.
[07:45] [09:10] Diego: load approaching 10k—p95 rises to ~420ms, we trigger fallback to quantized model for low-cost tier, and we start prefetch for pinned sessions.
[09:25] Alyssa: quick note: prefetch can help high-QPS hot prefixes but will increase memory; it's a tradeoff between latency and cost.
[09:34] Tom: are there metrics that show per-tenant cache hit ratio and cost delta?
[09:39] Diego: yes, console shows per-tenant cache hit, kv miss rate, and per-token cost overlay. i'll pull the CSV. (shares chart)
[09:50] Priya: the chart label says 'kv cash' in one place—typo?
[09:54] Diego: yeah our OCR on older dashboards had a label mistake, we'll fix that—thanks.
[10:02] [11:40] Diego: looking deeper, we have a session that hit 52k tokens; kv miss spikes as that session rotates between workers. to avoid jitter we recommend session-affinity by shard.
[11:55] Priya: can you assign affinity per-tenant or per-session?
[12:00] Diego: both; per-tenant affinity is default for Dedicated pools. per-session affinity can be used for very large conversational contexts. downside: it reduces packing efficiency.
[12:12] Tom: what about concurrency limits per client? if one session hogs KV, will you prevent it from starving others?
[12:19] Diego: yes we enforce per-session token budget and soft throttles; when a session exceeds budget, we either reject new turn or stream a 'degraded' answer. policy is configurable.
[12:30] Priya: show the policy UI.
[12:33] Diego: (navigates) policy -> quotas -> per-session token budget = 200k tokens / 24h for this demo. I'll lower for the run so we can observe.
[12:43] [14:05] Diego: lowering per-session budget now to 60k; that should cause excessive sessions to be soft-throttled.
[14:12] Evan: what does soft-throttle look like client-side? is it 429 or slower stream?
[14:18] Diego: we emit 429 if the request would exceed hard quota; soft throttle returns a 200 with a 'degraded' flag and shorter answer, plus a Retry-After header if applicable.
[14:31] Priya: hmm, mobile SDKs expect http2 streams; how do you signal degraded?
[14:36] Diego: two options: structured metadata in the initial response chunk or a trailing header. SDKs can surface a small inline banner or fallback UX.
[14:45] [16:10] Diego: we've now observed backpressure pathways—one of the streaming clients couldn't keep up and we moved it to resumable token path; its visible latency for resume was ~280ms. overall p95 for non-degraded sessions came back to ~360ms.
[16:28] Alyssa: note that your SLO target of 300ms p95 will be achievable with dedicated capacity and tuned prefetch/pinning; hosted burst mode is cheaper but you'll see more variability.
[16:41] Tom: cost delta? show ballpark.
[16:44] Alyssa: on our sample workload, dedicated pool with pinning yields ~18% higher per-token infra but reduces latency variance and dropped-streams by ~90%. we'll send a cost model.
[16:58] [18:00] Priya: security question: when you compact KV into a summary, is any PII ever persisted outside tenant blob storage? we need guarantee that nothing leaves customer-controlled stores.
[18:11] Diego: for Private deployments we can persist snapshots to your object store and use your KMS for envelope keys. for hosted, we encrypt at rest with per-tenant keys; compaction runs inside the same tenant sandbox. we'll share the HSM/KMS integration doc.
[18:28] Rita: do you have audit logs for eviction/compaction events?
[18:33] Alyssa: yes, audit trail includes eviction, TTL changes, pin/unpin, and fallback model routing, with timestamps. we can export to SIEM.
[18:43] [20:05] Priya: a failure mode: what if the shard autoscaler thrashes when many sessions are pinned then unpinned quickly? we saw this on our internal infra.
[20:16] Diego: we use hysteresis: a cooldown window, and node draining uses live migration where KV is offloaded to object store instead of immediate eviction. this avoids churn.
[20:28] Tom: can we test that during the pilot?
[20:32] Alyssa: yes, we can script a spike/unpin scenario as part of the 48-hour window.
[20:40] [22:00] Diego: final quick notes on Optimize: our suggestions engine can recommend min_recent_tokens, compaction_window, and autoscale thresholds based on observed token distributions. it generates a YAML you can apply to your Dedicated pool.
[22:15] Priya: will optimize respect private deployment constraints?
[22:19] Diego: yes, it runs offline against sample traces you upload; we don't ship your traces out.
[22:28] Alyssa: ok logging next steps: we'll share pricing, diego will post the tuning checklist link (https://redwood.example/pilot-kv-cheatsheet), priya you'll share traffic CSV.
[22:40] Priya: noted. two last questions: does your streaming TTL default vary by region? we've seen regional variance before.
[22:48] Diego: default is global but you can override per-region via the console.
[22:55] Evan: and the last: how do you measure 'quality delta' when falling back models? we need automatic regression alerts.
[23:03] Diego: Optimize integrates with evals—you can define prompts/metrics and alert on semantic drift or token-level BLEU-like metrics; we can tie alerts to rollbacks.
[23:20] Alyssa: great. any other blockers?
[23:25] Priya: nothing else for now. thanks that's very thorough.
[23:30] Alyssa: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and pilot plan.
[23:35] Tom: thanks. bye.
[23:40] [end of recording]
